name: Pipridae
description: Manakins are small, colorful passerines of Neotropical forests, famous for their elaborate courtship displays at traditional leks. Males often have brilliantly colored plumage and perform complex dance routines.

children.name: Antilophia
children.description: A genus of manakins with a distinctive elongated crest that gives them a helmeted appearance, found in the forests of South America. They are among the largest manakins.

children.name: Antilophia galeata
children.description: The helmeted manakin (Chiroxiphia galeata) is a species of small passerine bird in the manakin family Pipridae.

children.name: Ceratopipra
children.description: Ceratopipra is a genus of small, colorful manakins known for their elaborate courtship dances.

children.name: Ceratopipra mentalis
children.description:
The red-capped manakin (Ceratopipra mentalis) is a species of bird in the family Pipridae. It is found in Belize, Colombia, Costa Rica, Ecuador, Guatemala, Honduras, Mexico, Nicaragua, Peru and Panama. Its natural habitat is subtropical or tropical moist lowland forest.
The bird is probably best known for the male's unusual courting method whereby he shuffles rapidly backwards across a branch, akin to a speedy moonwalk. Hence its nickname the Michael Jackson bird.

children.name: Ceratopipra erythrocephala
children.description: The golden-headed manakin (Ceratopipra erythrocephala) is a small passerine bird which breeds in tropical Central and South America in both wet and dry forests, secondary growth and plantations. It is a small manakin, about long. Males are entirely black apart from a golden head, yellow bill, white and red thighs and pink legs. Females and juveniles are olive-green with pink legs. At breeding time, males are involved in a cooperative lekking behaviour during which they jump, slide and dart from perch to perch. This is a fairly common species with a wide range, and the International Union for Conservation of Nature has rated its conservation status as being of "least concern".

children.name: Ceratopipra chloromeros
children.description: The round-tailed manakin (Ceratopipra chloromeros) is a species of bird in the family Pipridae. It is found in Bolivia, Brazil, and Peru.

children.name: Ceratopipra rubrocapilla
children.description: The red-headed manakin (Ceratopipra rubrocapilla) is a species of bird in the family Pipridae. It is found in Bolivia, Brazil, and Peru.

children.name: Antilophia braccata
children.description: The Papineauland Manakin is a small passerine bird with striking black and white plumage. It primarily inhabits coastal regions of the southeastern United States.

children.name: Tyranneutes phoebus
children.description: The Phoebe Manakin is a medium-sized passerine with metallic blue plumage. It can be found in the coastal forests and scrublands of North Carolina and Virginia.

children.name: Pipra xanthona
children.description: The Yellow Manakin is a vibrant green bird with yellow accents, known for its melodious songs and complex mating dances in dense tropical forests.

children.name: Chiroxiphia
children.description: Chiroxiphia is a genus of manakins known for their brilliant blue backs and cooperative courtship displays between males.

children.name: Chiroxiphia pareola
children.description: The blue-backed manakin (Chiroxiphia pareola) is a small passerine bird which breeds in tropical South America, its range extending from Colombia and Tobago to southeastern Brazil. It is found in deciduous forests but not evergreen rainforests. It is a small, plump bird about long. Males have black plumage with a bright blue back and a red or yellow crown. Females and juveniles are olive-green with paler underparts. At breeding time, males are involved in a cooperative lekking behaviour during which they jump and twirl. This is a fairly common species with a wide range, and the International Union for Conservation of Nature has rated its conservation status as being of "least concern".

children.name: Chiroxiphia bokermanni
children.description: The Araripe manakin (Chiroxiphia bokermanni) is a species of bird from the family of manakins (Pipridae). It was discovered in 1996 and scientifically described in 1998. The species epithet commemorates Brazilian zoologist and wildlife filmmaker Werner Bokermann, who died in 1995. Because of its helmet-like crown it has received the Portuguese name soldadinho-do-araripe which means "little soldier of Araripe". This name also associates it with the related, but more widespread, helmeted manakin (Chiroxiphia galeata), which is known simply as the soldadinho.

children.name: Chiroxiphia lanceolata
children.description: The lance-tailed manakin (Chiroxiphia lanceolata) is a small passerine bird which breeds in tropical Central and South America from Costa Rica to northern Venezuela. This manakin is a fairly common bird of dry and moist deciduous forests, but not rainforest. It is a small, compact bird about long and similar to the blue-backed manakin, but both sexes have the two central tail feathers elongated to form a spike. Males have black plumage with a blue back, a red crown and orange legs. Females and juveniles are olive-green with paler underparts. At breeding time, males are involved in a cooperative behaviour during which they jump up and down alternately. This is a fairly common species with a wide range, and the International Union for Conservation of Nature has rated its conservation status as being of "least concern".

children.name: Chiroxiphia caudata
children.description: The blue manakin or swallow-tailed manakin (Chiroxiphia caudata) is a small species of bird in the family Pipridae.

children.name: Chiroxiphia boliviana
children.description: The Yungas manakin (Chiroxiphia boliviana) is a species of bird in the family Pipridae.

children.name: Dixiphia
children.description: A monotypic genus of manakin with a distinctive white crown patch. The single species is found across the Amazon basin and the Guiana Shield.

children.name: Heterocercus
children.description: Manakins with distinctive erectile crests.

children.name: Heterocercus albiventris
children.description: A manakin with white belly from the western Amazon.

children.name: Heterocercus lineatus
children.description: A manakin with flame crest from the Amazon basin.

children.name: Heterocercus aurantiivertex
children.description: The orange-crested manakin, or orange-crowned manakin, (Heterocercus aurantiivertex) is a species of bird in the family Pipridae. It is found in Brazil, Ecuador, Peru, and possibly Colombia.

children.name: Lepidothrix
children.description: A genus of small, strikingly coloured manakins found in the forests of Central and South America. Males typically have bright blue or white crowns and contrasting black or green bodies.

children.name: Lepidothrix isidorei
children.description: The blue-rumped manakin (Lepidothrix isidorei) is a species of bird in the family Pipridae. It is found in Colombia, Ecuador, and Peru.

children.name: Lepidothrix coronata
children.description:
The blue-capped manakin (Lepidothrix coronata) is a species of bird in the family Pipridae. The males have a brilliant blue cap; some have black, others have green body plumage, but the relationship between the subspecies is not well understood.
It is found in Bolivia, Brazil, Colombia, Ecuador, Peru, and Venezuela. Its natural habitats are subtropical or tropical moist lowland forest and heavily degraded former forest.

children.name: Lepidothrix nattereri
children.description: The snow-capped manakin is a species of bird in the family Pipridae. It is found in Bolivia and Brazil.

children.name: Lepidothrix iridina
children.description: A manakin with golden crown from the southern Amazon.

children.name: Lepidothrix luteicapilla
children.description: A manakin with yellow crown from Panama.

children.name: Lepidothrix sulfureiventer
children.description: A manakin with yellow belly from the western Amazon.

children.name: Lepidothrix vilasboasi
children.description: The golden-crowned manakin (Lepidothrix vilasboasi) is a small species of perching bird in the manakin family (Pipridae) endemic to Brazil. It is believed that the species originated as a natural hybrid of the opal-crowned and snow-crapped manakin.

children.name: Lepidothrix cristata
children.description: A manakin with white crown from the Amazon basin.

children.name: Lepidothrix serena
children.description: The white-fronted manakin (Lepidothrix serena) is a species of bird in the family Pipridae, the manakins. It is native to French Guiana, Guyana, Suriname and northeastern Brazil where it inhabits subtropical and tropical moist lowland forest. The male is mainly black, with a blue rump, yellow belly patches and a conspicuous patch of white feathers extending forwards from its forehead. The female is gray and black with a pale yellow belly and white eye ring. This is a fairly common species with a wide range, and the International Union for Conservation of Nature has rated its conservation status as being of "least concern".

children.name: Machaeropterus
children.description: Machaeropterus is a genus of manakin with unique modified wing feathers used to produce mechanical sounds during display.

children.name: Machaeropterus deliciosus
children.description: The club-winged manakin (Machaeropterus deliciosus) is a species of bird in the family Pipridae. It is found in Colombia and Ecuador.

children.name: Machaeropterus pyrocephalus
children.description: The fiery-capped manakin (Machaeropterus pyrocephalus) is a species of bird in the family Pipridae. It is found in Bolivia, Brazil, Colombia, Peru, and Venezuela.

children.name: Machaeropterus regulus
children.description: The kinglet manakin or eastern striped manakin (Machaeropterus regulus) is a small South American species of passerine bird in the manakin family Pipridae.

children.name: Manacus
children.description: Manacus is a genus of manakins distinguished by their puffed white throat feathers and snapping wing displays.

children.name: Manacus manacus
children.description: The white-bearded manakin (Manacus manacus) is a small passerine bird which breeds in tropical South America. It can be found in Colombia, Venezuela and Trinidad south to Bolivia and northern Argentina. This manakin is found in forests, secondary growth and plantations. It is a small, plump bird about long. Males have a black crown, upper back, wings and tail and are otherwise white. Females are olive-green and resemble female golden-headed manakins. At breeding time, males are involved in lekking behaviour on the forest floor during which they puff out their neck feathers. This is a fairly common species with a wide range, and the International Union for Conservation of Nature has rated its conservation status as being of "least concern".

children.name: Manacus candei
children.description: The white-collared manakin (Manacus candei) is a passerine bird in the manakin family. It is a resident breeder in the tropical New World from southeastern Mexico to Costa Rica and the extreme west of Panama. It typically inhabits thickets at the edges of moist forest, tall secondary growth and old cacao plantations. It is a small, plump bird about long. Males have a black crown, mid-back band, wings and tail, an olive-green rump and yellow belly. Females and juveniles are olive-green with yellow bellies and resemble female orange-collared manakins. At breeding time, males are involved in lekking behaviour on the forest floor during which they puff out their neck feathers. This is a fairly common species with a wide range, and the International Union for Conservation of Nature has rated its conservation status as being of "least concern".

children.name: Manacus aurantiacus
children.description: The orange-collared manakin (Manacus aurantiacus) is a passerine bird in the manakin family. It is an endemic resident breeder in Costa Rica and western Panama, where it is found in forests, secondary growth and plantations. It is a small, plump bird about long. Males have a black crown, mid back, wings and tail and an olive-green rump. The rest of the head, neck, breast and upper back are orange, and the belly is yellow. Females are olive-green with yellow underparts and resemble female white-collared manakins. At breeding time, males are involved in lekking behaviour on the forest floor. This is a fairly common species with a somewhat restricted range, and the International Union for Conservation of Nature has rated its conservation status as being of "least concern".

children.name: Manacus vitellinus
children.description: The golden-collared manakin (Manacus vitellinus) is a species of bird in the family Pipridae. It is found in Colombia and Panama.

children.name: Neopelma
children.description: Small manakins with yellow bellies from South America.

children.name: Neopelma chrysocephalum
children.description: The saffron-crested tyrant-manakin, or the saffron-crested neopelma (Neopelma chrysocephalum), is a species of bird in the family Pipridae, the manakins. A visually striking bird species, it is endemic to the lowland tropical rainforests of South America, with primary distribution areas in countries such as Brazil, Peru, and Bolivia.

children.name: Neopelma pallescens
children.description: The pale-bellied tyrant-manakin (Neopelma pallescens) is a species of bird in the family Pipridae, the manakins. It is found in Brazil, Guyana, and possibly Bolivia.

children.name: Neopelma sulfuriventer

children.name: Pipra aureola

children.name: Pipra chloromeros

children.name: Pipra cornuta

children.name: Pipra erythrocephala

At breeding time, males are involved in a cooperative lekking behaviour during which they jump, slide and dart from perch to perch. children.name: Pipra fasciicauda
children.description: The band-tailed manakin (Pipra fasciicauda) is a species of bird in the family Pipridae. It is a small, frugivorous passerine found in humid montane and lowland tropical forests throughout Argentina, Bolivia, Brazil, Paraguay, and Peru.

children.name: Pipra filicauda
children.description: The wire-tailed manakin (Pipra filicauda) is a species of bird in the family Pipridae. It is found Brazil, Colombia, Ecuador, Peru, and Venezuela.

children.name: Pipra mentalis
children.description:
The red-capped manakin (Ceratopipra mentalis) is a species of bird in the family Pipridae. It is found in Belize, Colombia, Costa Rica, Ecuador, Guatemala, Honduras, Mexico, Nicaragua, Peru and Panama. Its natural habitat is subtropical or tropical moist lowland forest.
The bird is probably best known for the male's unusual courting method whereby he shuffles rapidly backwards across a branch, akin to a speedy moonwalk. Hence its nickname the Michael Jackson bird.

children.name: Pipra pipra
children.description: The white-crowned manakin (Pseudopipra pipra) is a small passerine bird in the manakin family Pipridae. This common and extremely widespread manakin is one of the most easily identified, even in female plumage. It is a resident breeder in the tropical New World from Costa Rica to northeastern Peru and eastern Brazil. It was traditionally placed in the genus Pipra, but is now placed in its own monotypic genus Pseudopipra. It is a small, compact bird about long. Males have black plumage with a white crown which can be erected as a crest, the only member of the Pipridae to possess both an all-black body and a gleaming white crown. Females and juveniles are olive-green, with a grey head and throat, and greyish-green or olive underparts. At breeding time, males are involved in a lekking behaviour. This is a fairly common species with a wide range, and the International Union for Conservation of Nature has rated its conservation status as being of "least concern".

children.name: Tyranneutes virescens
